title: Our World, Years 1 to 3
subject: science
year_note: Written for the New Zealand Curriculum, Years 1 to 3 (Levels 1 to 2). Filed under science because most of it is the living world, weather and the senses, though it also carries safety and te reo words.
source_note: Written for the New Zealand Curriculum, Years 1 to 3 (Levels 1 to 2), ages 5 to 8. Covers days, months, southern hemisphere seasons, weather, the five senses, living and non-living things, farm and native animals, road and water safety, and everyday Te Reo Māori words. Te Reo words and macrons checked against general reference sources, 2026-08-30.

questions.prompt: How many days are in a week?
questions.explanation: A week has 7 days, from Monday through to Sunday.

questions.prompt: Which season comes after summer in New Zealand?
questions.explanation: In New Zealand the order is summer, autumn, winter, then spring.

questions.prompt: Which part of your body do you see with?
questions.explanation: You see with your eyes, one of your five senses.

questions.prompt: Which part of your body do you hear with?
questions.explanation: You hear with your ears, one of your five senses.

questions.prompt: Is a rock living or non-living?
questions.explanation: A rock does not grow, eat or breathe, so it is non-living.

questions.prompt: Is a dog living or non-living?
questions.explanation: A dog eats, grows and breathes, so it is living.

questions.prompt: What is New Zealand's national bird?
questions.explanation: The kiwi is New Zealand's national bird, and it cannot fly.

questions.prompt: What should you do before crossing the road?
questions.explanation: Always look both ways for cars before you cross the road.

questions.prompt: How many months are in a year?
questions.explanation: A year has 12 months, from January through to December.

questions.prompt: Which season is the coldest in New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Winter is the coldest season, and in New Zealand it falls in June, July and August.

questions.prompt: Which part of your body do you smell with?
questions.explanation: You smell with your nose, one of your five senses.

questions.prompt: Which part of your body do you taste with?
questions.explanation: You taste with your tongue, one of your five senses.

questions.prompt: Is a chair living or non-living?
questions.explanation: A chair does not grow, eat or breathe, so it is non-living.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a farm animal?
questions.explanation: A cow is a farm animal. The others are native New Zealand animals.

questions.prompt: What falls from the sky when it rains?
questions.explanation: Rain is water falling from clouds in drops.

questions.prompt: What does 'kia ora' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Kia ora' is a Te Reo Māori greeting, often used to say hello.

questions.prompt: What does 'kai' mean in Te Reo Māori?
questions.explanation: 'Kai' is the Te Reo Māori word for food.

questions.prompt: Before you cross the road, whose hand should you hold?
questions.explanation: Hold an adult's hand so someone you trust is watching for cars too.

questions.prompt: Which season comes before winter in New Zealand?
questions.explanation: Autumn comes before winter in New Zealand, as the weather cools down.

questions.prompt: In New Zealand, summer includes which month?
questions.explanation: New Zealand's summer is December, January and February, unlike countries north of the equator.

questions.prompt: Which part of your body do you feel with?
questions.explanation: You feel touch with your skin, one of your five senses.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a native New Zealand bird?
questions.explanation: The tui is a native New Zealand bird. The others are farm animals.

questions.prompt: Which native insect is known for being one of the heaviest insects in the world?
questions.explanation: The weta is a large native New Zealand insect, and some kinds are unusually heavy.

questions.prompt: What does 'whānau' mean in Te Reo Māori?
questions.explanation: 'Whānau' is the Te Reo Māori word for family.

questions.prompt: What does 'moana' mean in Te Reo Māori?
questions.explanation: 'Moana' is the Te Reo Māori word for sea or ocean.

questions.prompt: What does 'awa' mean in Te Reo Māori?
questions.explanation: 'Awa' is the Te Reo Māori word for river.

questions.prompt: Which of these shows something is a living thing?
questions.explanation: Growing is something only living things do, unlike rocks, toys or metal.

questions.prompt: At the beach, where should you swim?
questions.explanation: Lifeguards watch the water between the flags, so that is the safest place to swim.

questions.prompt: What does 'maunga' mean in Te Reo Māori?
questions.explanation: 'Maunga' is the Te Reo Māori word for mountain.

questions.prompt: What does 'aroha' mean in Te Reo Māori?
questions.explanation: 'Aroha' is the Te Reo Māori word for love or compassion.

questions.prompt: Which native NZ bird is known for copying sounds it hears?
questions.explanation: The tui sings a complex song and can copy other sounds it hears.

questions.prompt: Which native NZ bird has long legs and lives near swamps?
questions.explanation: The pukeko has long legs and toes for walking through wet, swampy ground.

questions.prompt: Kiwi are unusual birds because they cannot do what?
questions.explanation: Kiwi are flightless birds, so they cannot fly like most other birds.

questions.prompt: In New Zealand, which month is in spring?
questions.explanation: New Zealand's spring is September, October and November.

questions.prompt: On a boat, what should you wear to stay safe in the water?
questions.explanation: A lifejacket helps keep you afloat if you end up in the water.

questions.prompt: Which of these uses your senses to notice the weather?
choices: feeling the wind on your skin
questions.explanation: Feeling the wind uses your sense of touch to notice what the weather is doing.

questions.prompt: Which country has opposite seasons to New Zealand?
questions.explanation: England is north of the equator, so when New Zealand has summer, England has winter.

questions.prompt: Why is a weta unusual compared to most insects?
choices: it is very heavy for an insect
questions.explanation: Some weta grow surprisingly heavy for an insect, which is why people notice them.

questions.prompt: Which is true of living things but not non-living things?
questions.explanation: Only living things need food to survive. Size, colour and location do not tell living and non-living apart.

questions.prompt: In New Zealand, which two months are both in spring?
questions.explanation: Spring in New Zealand runs from September through to November, so September and October are both spring months.
